Framework must derive hybrids from observed cross-family co-occurrence in historical runs + industrial sources. description: Justified hybrid asset-family combinations (RECOVERY_2026-05-10 §2 Asset Family Engine — Gap B). motor_061 (Asset Family Isolation Validator) blocks cross-family pattern activation by default. Hybrids listed here are EXEMPT from contamination block PROVIDED a justification trigger is present in the evidence. Without the trigger, the cross-family activation remains contamination.

rules.trigger_match: case_sensitive=false; trigger token must appear in any of: motor_007.target_definition_contract.facility_evidence_tokens, motor_007.target_definition_contract.process_evidence_tokens, or motor_054.industrial_evidence_register entries.
rules.secondary_can_unlock_patterns: When a hybrid is admitted, patterns from the secondary family's allowed_patterns are no longer flagged as contamination by motor_061 AF1_pattern_contamination — provided the pattern_id is listed in hybrid.shared_patterns.

hybrids.rationale: Dairy, meat, ready-meal and bakery facilities frequently combine cold-chain storage with on-site thermal processing (cook, pasteurize, retort, sanitation steam). Process heat and refrigeration coexist by design; flagging process patterns as contamination would block valid cross-system intelligence.
scope_allowed: thermal-duty hypothesis (process steam vs refrigeration share)
process-support risk (boiler / steam trap / compressed air on the process side)
permit-first routing (state environmental permits, air emissions)
VOC / wastewater discovery
joint sanitation / refrigeration load characterization
scope_prohibited: declaring resin / press / curing as dominant scenario (those are NOT food processing)
treating storage-only cold-chain as thermal-process manufacturing
process closure without metered process-heat duty
fair-comparison peer-set substitution to pure manufacturing
evidence_to_confirm: permit demonstrating process heat or sanitation steam
production line inventory (cook / pasteurize / retort / sanitize)
tad_impact: DO_NOT_RETROFIT_YET on refrigeration if process-heat duty unbounded

hybrids.rationale: Modern omnichannel DCs combine ambient, refrigerated and frozen zones in a single building. Cold-chain patterns apply to the conditioned zones without invalidating warehouse logic (MHE charging, dock cycles).
scope_allowed: refrigeration duty characterization for conditioned zones only
defrost / cold-chain status discovery
zoned thermal-boundary characterization
joint MHE charging + cold-chain analysis
scope_prohibited: treating entire facility as cold-chain (ambient zone misclassified)
applying cold-chain peer set on a primarily ambient DC
evidence_to_confirm: refrigerated / frozen zone area share above threshold
compressor inventory dedicated to cold zones
evidence_to_falsify: no refrigerated / frozen zones in the facility
refrigerated zone < threshold (treat as ambient with rare exception)
tad_impact: MEASURE zone-by-zone duty before retrofit logic
DEFER refrigeration-first CAPEX until zone share quantified

hybrids.rationale: Class-A office buildings increasingly house edge DC or telco hub tenants. The DC load and cooling topology must be characterized independently from the office HVAC schedule, but coexist in one asset.
scope_allowed: PUE composition characterization for DC zone only
cooling topology discovery (chilled water vs DX vs separate CRAC)
tenant boundary discovery (DC operator vs landlord)
submetering topology for DC vs office
scope_prohibited: applying datacenter peer set to entire building
treating office HVAC schedule as DC HVAC schedule
evidence_to_falsify: no dedicated cooling for server space
IT load below threshold (treat as office plug load)
tad_impact: MEASURE IT load and HVAC load independently
DO_NOT_UNDERWRITE_ENERGY_RETROFIT_YET on cooling until topology mapped

hybrids.rationale: Plants with attached finished-goods warehouses (FMCG, automotive Tier-1, building products) present both process loads and DC loads in one footprint. Warehouse patterns are legitimate when the DC is operationally distinct from production lines.
scope_allowed: MHE charging demand-peak hypothesis on DC zone
dock infiltration loss on DC zone
high-bay lighting waste on DC zone
joint manufacturing + DC peer-set construction
scope_prohibited: applying warehouse patterns to production lines
MHE retrofit recommendation when DC is < threshold of operational footprint
Treating production-side energy as DC-side energy
evidence_to_confirm: shipping dock count above warehouse threshold
evidence_to_falsify: no shipping DC operations on site
DC area < small share of total footprint
tad_impact: CLASSIFY DC zone and production zone separately
MEASURE charging profile only on DC side
DEFER warehouse-style CAPEX until production-vs-DC split mapped

hybrids.rationale: Mixed-use commercial buildings hosting supermarkets, food retail, or commercial kitchens carry refrigeration loads that dominate base electrical consumption. Refrigeration logic applies despite the dominant office/retail building envelope.
scope_allowed: refrigeration duty for grocer / kitchen zone
refrigerant inventory / integrity for retail food zone
compressor staging on retail refrigeration
tenant boundary discovery (grocer operator vs building landlord)
scope_prohibited: applying refrigeration logic to non-food retail tenants
claiming refrigeration retrofit savings without tenant boundary mapped
treating commercial building HVAC as refrigeration topology
evidence_to_confirm: supermarket / food retail tenant on lease
evidence_to_falsify: no food retail tenant in the building
refrigeration load below threshold of total consumption
tad_impact: PROHIBIT_ROI on refrigeration until tenant capture mapped
